title: Second norm bound for low-degree noise
statement: Let $P$ be a finite product probability space, let $k\in\mathbb N$, and let $c\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $1\le c$. If $f$ is a real-valued function whose product components of every order greater than $k$ vanish identically, then $\|T_c f\|_{2,P}\le c^k\|f\|_{2,P}$.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a finite product probability space with strictly positive coordinate weights summing to one
Every product component of $f$ indexed by a set of size greater than $k$ vanishes at every outcome
$f$ is a real-valued function on the product outcome space
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $c\ge1$, $k\in\mathbb N$, and $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ of degree at most $k$. Then $\|T_cf\|_{2,P}\le c^k\|f\|_{2,P}$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $h_S=\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}E_Uh$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ (the Hoeffding--Efron--Stein components); $T_a h=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}a^{|S|}h_S$ for every real rate $a$; $\|h\|_{p,P}=(\mathbb E_P|h|^p)^{1/p}$ for $p>0$; degree at most $k$ means $h_S=0$ for every $|S|>k$. The powers indexed by subset cardinalities are natural powers, including $0^0=1$.
